scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: In Kathmandu, a blood test usually goes like this.
lines.say: In Kathmandu, a blood test usually goes like this.

lines.raw: The doctor writes the tests on a slip.
lines.say: The doctor writes the tests on a slip.

lines.raw: You pay at the counter, give your blood sample in the morning, and the staff tell you to **collect the report** in the evening or the next day.
lines.say: You pay at the counter, give your blood sample in the morning, and the staff tell you to collect the report in the evening or the next day.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Notice that you leave with **two different papers**.
lines.say: Notice that you leave with two different papers.

lines.raw: The **bill** (receipt) says which tests you paid for and how much.
lines.say: The bill (receipt) says which tests you paid for and how much.

lines.raw: The **lab report** says what the tests **found**: your sugar level, your cholesterol, with the normal range printed next to each number.
lines.say: The lab report says what the tests found: your sugar level, your cholesterol, with the normal range printed next to each number.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Simple definition.
lines.say: Simple definition.

lines.raw: Lab data is the record of medical tests done on samples from your body (blood, urine and so on): which test was done, when, by whom, and what the result was.
lines.say: Lab data is the record of medical tests done on samples from your body (blood, urine and so on): which test was done, when, by whom, and what the result was.

lines.raw: Two kinds of lab data.
lines.say: Two kinds of lab data.

lines.raw: The bill and the report have twins in US data.
lines.say: The bill and the report have twins in U S data.

lines.raw: The bill becomes a **lab claim**.
lines.say: The bill becomes a lab claim.

lines.raw: The report becomes a **lab result**.
lines.say: The report becomes a lab result.

lines.raw: They travel on different roads and land in different tables.
lines.say: They travel on different roads and land in different tables.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Nepal twin. Lab claim: The bill / receipt from the counter. Lab result: The lab report you collect the next day.
lines.say: Nepal twin. Lab claim: The bill or receipt from the counter. Lab result: The lab report you collect the next day.

lines.raw: Answers. Lab claim: **Was** a test done, and how much did it cost? Lab result: **What did the test find?**.
lines.say: Answers. Lab claim: Was a test done, and how much did it cost? Lab result: What did the test find?.

lines.raw: Main code. Lab claim: CPT procedure code, e.g. `83036` (HbA1c test). Lab result: LOINC test code, e.g. `4548-4` (HbA1c).
lines.say: Main code. Lab claim: C P T procedure code, for example 8 3 0 3 6 (H b A 1 c test). Lab result: L O I N C test code, for example 4 5 4 8 dash 4 (H b A 1 c).

lines.raw: Has the actual number? Lab claim: **No**. Lab result: **Yes**, e.g. 9.4 %.
lines.say: Has the actual number? Lab claim: No. Lab result: Yes, for example 9.4 percent.

lines.raw: Sent by. Lab claim: The lab, to the insurer, to get paid. Lab result: The lab, to the doctor (and sometimes to the insurer).
lines.say: Sent by. Lab claim: The lab, to the insurer, to get paid. Lab result: The lab, to the doctor (and sometimes to the insurer).

lines.raw: Where it is covered. Lab claim: Lesson 3 (the Medical course covers claims in general). Lab result: Lessons 4 to 6.
lines.say: Where it is covered. Lab claim: Lesson 3 (the Medical course covers claims in general). Lab result: Lessons 4 to 6.

lines.raw: The big idea.
lines.say: The big idea.

lines.raw: A claim can tell you that Robert **had** his blood sugar tested.
lines.say: A claim can tell you that Robert had his blood sugar tested.

lines.raw: Only the result can tell you whether his sugar is **under control**.
lines.say: Only the result can tell you whether his sugar is under control.

lines.raw: For many questions about health, you need the result.
lines.say: For many questions about health, you need the result.

lines.raw: In Nepal: Ram and Sita get blood tests in Kathmandu.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: **Ram** takes a yearly health check-up package at a private hospital.
lines.say: Ram takes a yearly health check-up package at a private hospital.

lines.raw: He pays the whole bill at the counter.
lines.say: He pays the whole bill at the counter.

lines.raw: The next day he collects his report: blood sugar, cholesterol, kidney tests and more.
lines.say: The next day he collects his report: blood sugar, cholesterol, kidney tests and more.

lines.raw: To claim the money back, he sends the **bill** (and often a copy of the report) to his insurer.
lines.say: To claim the money back, he sends the bill (and often a copy of the report) to his insurer.

lines.raw: The insurer mainly cares about the bill.
lines.say: The insurer mainly cares about the bill.

lines.raw: The numbers stay on paper in Ram's file.
lines.say: The numbers stay on paper in Ram's file.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: **Sita** has her blood tested at an SSF-listed hospital as part of her treatment.
lines.say: Sita has her blood tested at an S S F listed hospital as part of her treatment.

lines.raw: She pays her **20%** share.
lines.say: She pays her 20 percent share.

lines.raw: The hospital includes the test in its **claim to SSF** for the other 80%.
lines.say: The hospital includes the test in its claim to S S F for the other 80 percent.

lines.raw: Sita gets her report from the hospital.
lines.say: Sita gets her report from the hospital.

lines.raw: In the US: Robert gets a blood test in Houston, USA.
lines.say: In the U S: Robert gets a blood test in Houston, U S A.

lines.raw: **Robert Carter** is Emily's father, a retired teacher born in 1957.
lines.say: Robert Carter is Emily's father, a retired teacher born in 1957.

lines.raw: He has **type 2 diabetes** and **high blood pressure**.
lines.say: He has type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure.

lines.raw: He has **Medicare** (the US government programme for people 65 and older) through **Gulf Coast Advantage (HMO)**, a fictional **Medicare Advantage** plan from **Gulf Coast Health Plan**: a private insurer that runs his Medicare benefits.
lines.say: He has Medicare (the U S government programme for people 65 and older) through Gulf Coast Advantage (H M O), a fictional Medicare Advantage plan from Gulf Coast Health Plan: a private insurer that runs his Medicare benefits.

lines.raw: His primary care doctor, **Dr. Nguyen** at **Bayou Family Medicine** (fictional), orders blood tests to check his diabetes and cholesterol.
lines.say: His primary care doctor, Doctor Nguyen at Bayou Family Medicine (fictional), orders blood tests to check his diabetes and cholesterol.

lines.raw: A nurse draws his blood on **10 February 2025**.
lines.say: A nurse draws his blood on 10 February 2025.

lines.raw: It goes to **Bayou Clinical Lab** (a fictional independent lab).
lines.say: It goes to Bayou Clinical Lab (a fictional independent lab).

lines.raw: The lab sends a **claim** to his plan to get paid, and sends the **results** electronically to Dr. Nguyen's computer system.
lines.say: The lab sends a claim to his plan to get paid, and sends the results electronically to Doctor Nguyen's computer system.

lines.raw: Who is involved?
lines.say: Who is involved?

lines.raw: The roles in one lab test.
lines.say: The roles in one lab test.

lines.raw: **Patient**. Who: The person tested. Robert's example: Robert Carter.
lines.say: Patient. Who: The person tested. Robert's example: Robert Carter.

lines.raw: **Ordering provider**. Who: The doctor who asks for the test. Robert's example: Dr. Nguyen, his primary care doctor.
lines.say: Ordering provider. Who: The doctor who asks for the test. Robert's example: Doctor Nguyen, his primary care doctor.

lines.raw: **Performing lab**. Who: The lab that runs the test on the sample. Robert's example: Bayou Clinical Lab.
lines.say: Performing lab. Who: The lab that runs the test on the sample. Robert's example: Bayou Clinical Lab.

lines.raw: **Payer**. Who: Who pays the lab's bill. Robert's example: Gulf Coast Health Plan (runs his Medicare Advantage plan, Gulf Coast Advantage).
lines.say: Payer. Who: Who pays the lab's bill. Robert's example: Gulf Coast Health Plan (runs his Medicare Advantage plan, Gulf Coast Advantage).

lines.raw: **Receiver of results**. Who: Who gets the numbers. Robert's example: Dr. Nguyen (and Robert, through the clinic's patient portal).
lines.say: Receiver of results. Who: Who gets the numbers. Robert's example: Doctor Nguyen (and Robert, through the clinic's patient portal).

lines.raw: Tests are done in different places: a big **independent lab** (with collection centres all over the city, much like the chain labs in Kathmandu), a **hospital lab**, or a small lab inside the **doctor's office**.
lines.say: Tests are done in different places: a big independent lab (with collection centres all over the city, much like the chain labs in Kathmandu), a hospital lab, or a small lab inside the doctor's office.

lines.raw: The place affects who sends the claim, but the result looks much the same.
lines.say: The place affects who sends the claim, but the result looks much the same.

lines.say: Where do insurers get lab results?

lines.raw: An insurer **always** gets the claim, because the lab wants to be paid.
lines.say: An insurer always gets the claim, because the lab wants to be paid.

lines.raw: Getting the **result** is harder.
lines.say: Getting the result is harder.

lines.raw: It needs an extra data feed.
lines.say: It needs an extra data feed.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Lab claims**. What it gives: Which test, which date, which lab, how much. No result. Nepal comparison: The receipt.
lines.say: Lab claims. What it gives: Which test, which date, which lab, how much. No result. Nepal comparison: The receipt.

lines.raw: **Lab result feeds**. What it gives: Electronic results sent by large labs to the insurer under an agreement. Nepal comparison: The lab emailing your report to your insurer.
lines.say: Lab result feeds. What it gives: Electronic results sent by large labs to the insurer under an agreement. Nepal comparison: The lab emailing your report to your insurer.

lines.raw: **Doctor's records (EHR)**. What it gives: Results stored in the doctor's electronic health record. Nepal comparison: The report in your hospital file.
lines.say: Doctor's records (E H R). What it gives: Results stored in the doctor's electronic health record. Nepal comparison: The report in your hospital file.

lines.raw: **Result codes on claims**. What it gives: A few special codes that say a result range, e.g. "HbA1c above 9%" (lesson 6). Nepal comparison: The doctor writing "sugar high" on the bill.
lines.say: Result codes on claims. What it gives: A few special codes that say a result range, for example "H b A 1 c above 9 percent" (lesson 6). Nepal comparison: The doctor writing "sugar high" on the bill.

lines.raw: Why do insurers care about results?
lines.say: Why do insurers care about results?

lines.raw: To measure **quality of care** (is a diabetic patient's sugar under control?), to find members who need **extra help** (care management), and to understand how sick their members are.
lines.say: To measure quality of care (is a diabetic patient's sugar under control?), to find members who need extra help (care management), and to understand how sick their members are.

lines.raw: Quality scores, such as the **HEDIS** measures (a national set of health plan quality measures) you will meet in lesson 7, often need the actual number.
